key_insight: A single-step, solvent-free polybromide melt can directly convert elemental metal films into optoelectronic-grade bromide perovskites at room temperature.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable, roll-to-roll-compatible route to fabricate perovskite films from metals without preforming specific oxidation states, simplifying manufacturing and improving process flexibility.
method: Methylammonium polybromide melt (PBM) is applied directly to elemental films of Pb, Sn, Au, and Cu.
The melt chemistry is tuned to control reactivity and suppress unwanted overoxidation, especially for Sn.
In situ XRD tracks transient intermediates and phase evolution during conversion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful room-temperature conversion to MAPbBr3, MASnBr3, MA2Au2Br6, and MA2CuBr4, including high-quality MASnBr3 under ambient conditions.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful control of PBM composition and redox balance; overly reactive conditions can drive overoxidation or undesired phase pathways.
paper_title: A Universal Polybromide Melt Strategy for the Direct Conversion of Metals into Optoelectronic-Grade Bromide Perovskites
